{{Quote|They're Adegan crystals&mdash;precious and hard to find. Jedi use them to make the best lightsabers.|[[Andur Sunrider]]|audio=AdeganCrystals-TOTJ.flac|<ref name="Tales of the Jedi (audio)">[[Tales of the Jedi (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
'''Adegan crystals''' were a subset of [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|lightsaber crystal]] found in and around the [[Adega system/Legends|Adega system]].<ref name="Force Destiny Core" /> The most common lightsaber crystal in the days of the Old Republic, they were used by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] for thousands of years as a main component of a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]].<ref name="JATM" /> 

==History==

Adegan crystals were first discovered long ago on the planet [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] in the Adega system, by the inhabitants of an ancient Jedi stronghold.<ref name="FF 119" /> 

Prior to the discovery of [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]], the vast majority of lightsaber crystals originated in the Adega system.<ref name="JATM" /> As a result, the name "Adegan crystal" was commonly applied to all such crystals,<ref name="DE endnotes" /> including those found on [[Halm]],<ref>''[[Star Wars: Yoda Stories]]''</ref> [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the [[Cularin asteroid belt]],<ref>{{LivingForce|Jedi Code: The Way of the Force}}</ref> and later, Ilum itself.<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> 

The [[Mephite crystal/Legends|mephite]] and [[Pontite crystal/Legends|pontite]] variants of Adegan crystals, which produced the best lightsaber blades, were similar in structure to [[Ilum crystal/Legends|Ilum crystals]]. However, crystals from Ilum were much more common, while Adegan crystals were rare even in their own system.<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> 

During the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor Palpatine]] obstructed acquisition of all crystals capable of use in a lightsaber, by closing off or destroying all known sources, and having his agents remove as many as possible from circulation.<ref name="Force Destiny Core" />

==Properties==
The Force shared a special connection with Adegan crystals, and it was through their use that Jedi created a bond amongst themselves, the Force, and their weapon. This trait caused the Adegan crystals in a lightsaber to give off a weak Force signature that could be sensed by any Jedi.<ref name="Force Destiny Core" />

When induced by resonant frequencies, the crystals emitted powerful bursts of light, and further components of a lightsaber harnessed this power into a rod-like beam.<ref name="DE endnotes" />

==Types of Adegan crystal==
[[File:Pontites.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A cache of rare pontite crystals]]
*[[Kathracite crystal/Legends|Kathracite]] was the most common form of Adegan crystal, followed by [[Relacite/Legends|relacite]] and [[Danite/Legends|danite]]. These crystals didn't focus energy as well as their rarer cousins, and thus were usually reserved for use in training sabers.
*[[Mephite crystal/Legends|Mephite]] was a typical Adegan crystal used by the Jedi.
*[[Pontite crystal/Legends|Pontite]] was the rarest and most powerful type of Adegan crystal. Nearly impossible to find, it resonated with a powerful aura that cooled both skin and temperament.<ref name="KotOR2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The term "Adegan crystal" was created by writer [[Tom Veitch]] in the ''[[Dark Empire]]'' [[Dark Empire endnotes|endnotes]], as an alternative name for all naturally-formed lightsaber crystals, after the system in which they were most commonly found.<ref name="DE endnotes" /> In revised endnotes, the broader term "Ilum crystal" was introduced as a generic name for all crystals, thus making the terms Adegan, Ilum and lightsaber crystal synonymous.<ref name="DE endnotes 93"> [[Dark Empire endnotes|''Dark Empire'' endnotes]] {{C|[[1993]] 1st ed. and [[1995]] 2nd ed. [[Star Wars: Dark Empire (trade paperback)|TPB]]}}</ref> However, with the later introduction of a crystal-rich planet called Ilum into [[Star Wars Legends|continuity]],<ref>''[[Jedi Quest: Path to Truth]]''</ref> an in-universe explanation was provided for the terms being used interchangably, namely that crystals from the newly discovered Ilum were so similar in structure to variants from the Adegan system, that the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] took them to be the same at first.<ref name="JATM" />
